title: Intarsia animal baby blanket
subtitle: A 75 by 90 cm cot blanket with a central intarsia animal motif in DK on 4 mm needles.
excerpt: A 75 by 90 cm cot blanket in DK with a central 40-stitch by 50-row intarsia duck or bunny motif on a stocking-stitch ground. Intarsia uses separate yarn bobbins for each colour block; no stranding. About 240 g of the main colour and 30 g of the motif colour.
sourceNotes: Weldon's Practical Knitter, 8th series (1892), §Intarsia Nursery Work, describes intarsia (separate-bobbin block colour) as the standard method for animal motifs in baby blankets. The duck and bunny motifs given here use simple silhouette shapes derivable from grid paper.

knitting.gaugeText: 22 sts × 30 rows = 10 × 10 cm in stocking stitch on 4 mm needles, blocked.

glossaryTerms.definition: A colour knitting technique where each distinct colour block uses a separate length of yarn (wound onto a small bobbin or cut and left hanging). Unlike stranded colourwork, the yarns are not carried across the wrong side; they hang at the boundary of each colour block and are twisted together at each colour change to link the blocks and prevent holes. Best for large solid colour areas.

content.text: A single-panel rectangle worked flat on 4 mm needles with a central 40-stitch by 50-row animal motif worked in
intarsia
, finishing at 75 cm wide by 90 cm long.

Single-panel construction; no seaming. The stocking-stitch ground is worked in the main colour throughout; the motif colour is introduced only within the central 40 stitches over rows 60 to 110 (positioning the motif near the centre of the blanket). Intarsia uses a separate small bobbin of motif-colour yarn rather than stranding it across the back; no long floats are created. The blanket needs wet blocking to flatten the stocking-stitch ground. Budget about 240 g of main colour (about 528 m / 577 yards) and 30 g of motif colour (about 66 m / 72 yards).
What you need

items.name: Main colour (MC)
items.qty: 240 g (about 528 m / 577 yards) of DK-weight machine-washable yarn

items.name: Motif colour (CC)
items.qty: 30 g (about 66 m / 72 yards) of DK in a bold contrast colour

items.name: Needles
items.qty: 4 mm (UK 8 / US 6) circular needle, 80 cm or longer

content.text: Gauge
22 stitches and 30 rows to 10 cm in stocking stitch on 4 mm needles. The motif region is also stocking stitch; intarsia does not change gauge.
The duck motif is 40 stitches wide (about 18 cm) and 50 rows tall (about 17 cm), centred in the blanket width and height.
Stitches used

items.name: twist
items.qty: at each colour-change boundary: wrap the incoming yarn around the outgoing yarn once to link the blocks

content.text: Pattern
Cast-on
Using MC and the long-tail cast-on, cast on 165 stitches. Long-tail tail: (4 × 165) / 10 + 15 = 66 + 15 = 81 cm. Measure 95 cm.
Ground (rows 1 to 59)
Using MC only, work stocking stitch (k RS, p WS) for 59 rows. This positions the motif bottom edge at approximately 20 cm from the cast-on, placing it slightly below centre.
Motif section (rows 60 to 109)

The motif occupies stitches 63 to 102 (40 stitches centred in the 165-stitch width: (165 - 40) / 2 = 62.5, round to 63). On each RS row: k62 MC, work 40 motif stitches from chart (CC for the duck/bunny silhouette, MC for the ground within the motif zone), k63 MC. At each MC-CC boundary, twist the yarns once to close the gap. Wind the CC yarn on a small bobbin to prevent tangling. The duck motif chart is a simple silhouette grid: trace a 40×50 grid and fill in the duck outline in CC and the surrounding ground in MC.
Upper ground (rows 110 to end)
Cut CC yarn (leave 15 cm tail). Return to MC only and work stocking stitch until the blanket measures 90 cm from the cast-on edge.
Stitch count check-ins
At row 135 (about 45 cm, within the motif zone): count across. You should have 165 stitches. Intarsia does not change the stitch count. At row 268 (about 89.5 cm): count again before casting off.
Common faults

Hole at the colour-change boundary: the yarns were not twisted at the transition point. On every RS and WS row, the incoming colour must wrap around the outgoing colour once before the first stitch of the new colour is worked.

Motif colour stranded across the wrong side rather than worked intarsia: CC was carried across all 40 stitches rather than only used within the motif and left hanging at the boundary. The motif section should have the CC bobbin hanging from the last CC stitch, not running horizontally across the wrong side.
Cast-off
Cast off knitwise with MC, with a relaxed tension.
Finishing
Weave in all MC and CC tails on the wrong side. Wet block the finished blanket to flatten the stocking-stitch ground and even the motif edges.
Care
Machine wash on a gentle 30-degree cycle for superwash DK. Lay flat to dry, reshaping to measurements.
What to try next

From a single intarsia motif, try multiple intarsia blocks: three smaller motifs (star, heart, moon) on the same blanket, each worked from its own bobbin set. The technique is identical; only the number of active colour zones increases.
